title: Mini Win — Check What You Learned
summary: Small and shipped beats complete and untested — Mini Win before perfection

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.subtitle: Beginning of the Lesson
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What will you understand? ‘Small and shipped’ is better than ‘complete and untested’ — Mini Win before perfection.
- Why now? You have completed 3 layers: Frontend, Backend, Database. It's time to pause and solidify.
- What comes after the lesson? You will define Mini Win for your app — the smallest version you can publish and test.

sections.heading: Tension
sections.subtitle: Planning for a Huge App — and Not Starting
sections.contentMarkdown:
- You have 20 features in mind: login, payment, 5 languages, dashboard, notifications...
- After a month, you are still planning — and nothing works in front of a real user.
- The problem is not the idea. The problem is that you are waiting for ‘perfection’ before trying.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.subtitle: Small and Shipped > Complete and Untested
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Mini Win = the smallest version of your app that you publish and test with a real user.
- One page + one action + one result = enough to start.
- Feedback from 3 users is more valuable than 30 features that no one has tried.
- Phase 2 completed the concepts — Phase 3 will build. Mini Win is your bridge.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.subtitle: Full App in Mind vs Mini Win
sections.contentMarkdown:
| ‘I will do everything first’ | Mini Win in a Week |
|----------------------|-------------------|
| 3 months of planning. login + payment + 10 pages. No one tried it — no feedback | One page: write a question → AI responds. 5 friends tried it. I learned what works and what doesn’t |

sections.heading: Glossary
sections.subtitle: Two Terms to Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| Mini Win | The smallest published version that proves the idea works — not a prototype in your mind | ‘AI summarizes an article’ — one page, paste + button + summary. That’s it |
| MVP (Minimum Viable Product) | The same idea in English — the smallest product that delivers real value | Uber started with ‘request a car’ — without Uber Eats |

sections.heading: Core Block
sections.subtitle: 3 Layers Ready to Build
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Frontend: the client sees and clicks.
- Backend: AI works behind the screen.
- Database: the app remembers.
- Mini Win = the least in every layer — but it works end-to-end.

sections.heading: Quiz
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: Sara has an idea for an AI app with 15 features. What is the best step before Phase 3?
Define Mini Win — the smallest version you can publish and test.
Complete planning all 15 features.
Learn React and SQL first.
Explanation: Mini Win first — real feedback is more important than a complete plan without testing.

sections.heading: Mission
sections.subtitle: Define Mini Win for Your App
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: Definition mission — not building. Use the Product Request from the transition lesson. 5–10 minutes. Delivery: 1. The idea (sentence)
2. Mini Win: one page, one action, one result
3. What is not in Mini Win (later): feature 1, feature 2
4. First 3 testers Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Defined Mini Win | 60% | Page + action + result — not a ‘complete app’. You can imagine it published in a week |
| Clear boundaries | 40% | Includes ‘not now’. 3 testers defined |
